14:א: (49) By a korah — so that through it there will be recognition that they should not come to confuse and carry in a full reshus ha-rabbim, and also that they should not come to carry from it outward:
14:ב: (50) On the head of the mavo — meaning at the end of the mavo; and if he placed it in the middle of the mavo, see below in seif 362:
14:ג: (51) But if he drove, etc. — meaning that he inserted two pegs into the two walls on this side and that toward reshus ha-rabbim; and what is written "even close to it" means the pegs were very short, and automatically when he placed the korah on them it was close to the walls without any gap between them — nevertheless it is invalid; and the reason is that for a korah on walls we require that it not appear that it came to qualify the mavo, but only when it is within the hollow of the mavo, for it is not the way of any ceiling or korah to place it except on the walls and not from outside; and specifically for korah, but for lechi we do not require within the hollow of the mavo, but even outside the hollow of the mavo, and like that case of seif 13 above; and the reason of the matter is that a lechi, even standing outside, is recognizable that it came to qualify the mavo, unlike a korah, as explained:
14:ד: (52) Invalid — and if he drove two pegs into the ground close to the mavo walls on this side and that from outside and placed the korah on them, it is valid because of lechi [Or Zarua and R' Akiva Eiger and Shach]:
15:א: (53) But if not, etc. — like one who places a korah from wall to wall to strengthen the walls, and all similar cases:
15:ב: (54) Even if they relied on it, etc. — and although for lechi we hold in seif 12 that if they relied on it from erev Shabbat it helps even when standing by itself — there it is different, for lechi is because of partition, and a partition standing by itself is also a partition; but a korah is because of recognition, and when it was not placed for that purpose there is no recognition; and see Peri Megadim who sides that even if the korah were four tefachim wide it also does not help; and see Biur Halacha:
16:א: (55) Requires measure — as below in seif 17:
16:ב: (56) And therefore, etc. — and the same for anything that requires measure, such as what was mentioned above in seif 2, a pas of four tefachim on one side, or one tefach from here and one tefach from here:
16:ג: (57) From asherah wood — that a Jew worked it so it has no nullification, or even of a gentile and a Jew cut it [for if a gentile cut it, behold it was nullified automatically, as stated in Yoreh De'ah siman 146 seif 6], and the Jew took it for his benefit, for by this gentile property becomes Israel property that has no nullification; therefore we say cut down its measure applies to it; but if the Jew did not take it for his benefit, it is gentile property of a gentile that has nullification, and since it has nullification we do not say cut down its measure, even before it was nullified:
17:א: (58) One tefach wide — and although it requires measure to receive upon it a brick that is one tefach and a half wide, one can join a quarter tefach from it in mortar here and a quarter tefach from it there [Gemara]:
17:ב: (59) To receive a brick, etc. — meaning bricks, each of which holds in its length three tefachim and in its width one tefach and a half, lying upon it along its entire length as the measure of the width of that mavo's opening [and nevertheless, if the mavo opening was ten amot wide, it need not be fit to receive bricks along its entire length; rather it suffices if it can receive bricks along a length of nine amot and two mashehuyin, which are eighteen bricks in their length, for a korah of nine amot and two mashehuyin permits a mavo of width ten amot by the law of lavud — meaning that it should not reach less than three tefachim to this wall and less than three tefachim to that wall, as below in siman 361]; and the reason it must be fit to receive bricks is that otherwise there would not be so much recognition that people of reshus ha-rabbim would think they placed it there temporarily; but when it is healthy and strong to receive such building, it is recognizable to all that building placement was intended for this purpose:
18:א: (60) That are not one tefach wide, etc. — for otherwise those placing them would themselves have the status of korah upon them, and also their length would not be three so that the korah would be lavud to the wall, as all explained in siman 365:
18:ב: (61) And to support half a brick — and as explained in seif 17:
18:ג: (62) Rather only to support it — for one does not place bricks upon it; and for korah we require permanence so that there be excellent recognition, but the recognition does not depend on those placing it [Rashi]; and l'chatchila it is proper to be stringent like the first view:
19:_: (63) If the korah was round, etc. — and although now when it is round it cannot receive a brick upon it, nevertheless it is valid, for we consider it as if it were divided in two [Rashi]:
20:א: (64) Inclines outside the mavo, etc. — for all these matters disqualify a korah:
20:ב: (65) We view whatever if one removed, etc. — and the reason is that we say lavud:
20:ג: (66) And if not — it is invalid; meaning specifically in this manner, where part of the bent korah is outside the qualifying measure of the mavo; but if it is entirely within the mavo as required, even if the bend is much more than three tefachim, it is valid, for we say we view it as if it were straight [thus it is evident from Rambam's conclusion in chapter 17 law 26 see there, and likewise from other Rishonim; however in Sefer Gaon Yaakov and in Chiddushei Even HaEzer they question this, see there]:
21:א: (67) And it does not touch, etc. — and even if distant from the two walls in such a manner, such as if he drove a tree in the middle of the mavo and placed a korah on it, we say lavud from two directions:
21:ב: (68) Invalid — rather he must bring another korah, or see to fill that gap with a piece of korah:
22:א: (69) Meaning one tefach — meaning that together they should be one tefach wide:
22:ב: (70) And there are not three tefachim between them — we consider them as if adjacent to one another because of lavud:
22:ג: (71) And some say, etc. — they hold that lavud does not apply here to permit, for we require that the korah be fit to receive a brick in its width, and when they are far apart they cannot receive a brick upon them:
22:ד: (72) Within one tefach — for a brick in its width holds one tefach and a half, and there must be at least a quarter tefach leaning from it upon this korah and a quarter upon the other; if so, the gap between them will not remain except the measure of one tefach and no more:
23:א: (73) If it was, etc. — here he comes to add a leniency on the previous seif, that even if the two korot that cannot each receive a brick were not standing level but one was higher than its fellow up to three tefachim, it is also valid, for we say we view, etc.:
23:ב: (74) And the lower one, etc. — meaning, or the lower one [Rashi]:
23:ג: (75) Provided, etc. — twenty; for if it is above twenty, then even if the lower one is adjacent to it within three tefachim, we do not say as if it were below twenty, since now it stands in an invalid place; and likewise if the lower one is below ten and the upper is adjacent within three tefachim, we do not say we view the lower as if standing level with the upper, since now it has no korah qualification:
23:ד: (76) With intent — meaning aligned; and this is that even if we consider that this one already descended somewhat and the lower one ascended somewhat until they became opposite one another level, they would then be distant only less than three tefachim, for then lavud applies, as likewise in the previous seif in the first view:
23:ה: (77) And some disqualify — because they hold we do not say we view the upper, etc.; and although below in the laws of sukkah in siman 631 the Mechaber ruled plainly in seif 5 that if the s'chach is mixed and one above and one below, if there are not three tefachim between them we say lavud — here it is different, for we require that they be fit to receive a brick, and with one above and one below they are not fit to receive a brick [Or Zarua]; and this is that even if they are one tefach higher than one another it also does not help; and even if standing exactly level, this view holds like the second view above, that we require specifically that they be adjacent to one another, not more than one tefach; and Avraham Rabba wrote one should be stringent like this view:
24:א: (78) A mat — that he wished to strengthen the permission and spread a mat over it, and also tied it to the wall so wind would not move it, so that there would also be a partition name upon it:
24:ב: (79) Invalid — even if the mat itself is ten high:
24:ג: (80) And it is not visible — if so there is no recognition here:
24:ד: (81) A wide korah — meaning that it is ten tefachim wide; and one might have thought that since it is so wide, a partition name is upon it and not a korah name, and a partition is not valid when it is high from the ground greatly, like a mat — it informs us that it is valid, for because of its greatness the korah name was not nullified from it; and a mat is different, for it covered the korah and it is not recognizable:
24:ה: (82) And extends somewhat below ten — several Acharonim questioned his words, for it appears from his wording that he comes to inform us that even part of the wide korah enters within the lower ten tefachim of the mavo, it is also valid, for we say we view this portion as if it were not there and the korah stands only above ten, as the korah qualification explained in siman 366; but in truth this is not so, for if part of the korah width entered within the airspace of the lower ten, it is invalid, for we require that the hollow of the mavo up to the korah be precisely ten tefachim:
25:א: (83) Bent on two, etc. — meaning that the pegs stood on the two sides on a slope and their heads protrude above the height of the walls:
25:ב: (84) And he placed the korah on them — meaning, and here there are two deficiencies: first, the korah is not placed on the wall itself but only in the air above on the pegs; second, the korah is shorter than the area between the two walls:
25:ג: (85) And the pegs are not one tefach — for if the pegs were one tefach wide, we would not care that the korah itself is short, for the pegs themselves are counted as korah:
25:ד: (86) Valid, etc. — for in that the pegs are not higher than the mavo walls by three tefachim, we say throw it down, meaning as if the korah were knocked down and lowered to the walls; and even though it is still short, since the inclination of the pegs is not three, and therefore the korah is not distant three tefachim from the walls, we say lavud:
25:ה: (87) Invalid — for in the measure of three we do not say throw down for korah, nor lavud:
26:א: (88) When it is not low — meaning that if the ground in the mavo is not low from inside opposite the walls by the measure of ten tefachim, it is considered as if the mavo has no partitions, for there is no partition less than ten:
26:ב: (89) Spaced — and in the latter clause precise; for we go stringently everywhere for this matter. And the measure of spaced over precise is half a fingerbreadth per amah:
26:ג: (90) More than ten — for if it is more than ten it has no name of opening, and lechi and korah do not help for this:
26:ד: (91) Precise — meaning that for each amah its six tefachim are measured precise; and likewise in the latter clause for mavo length, for we require four amot spaced, it is likewise that its tefachim are measured spaced; if so, two fingerbreadths are added to the four amot, as explained:
26:ה: (92) Its length four amot, etc. — for in less than this measure it is not considered a mavo but as a courtyard:
26:ו: (93) Only by tzurat hapetach — meaning that even if it was low less than ten tefachim, tzurat hapetach also helps; and likewise if the width is ten amot, or if its length was not four amot; but many Acharonim agreed with the ruling that if the hollow of the mavo was low less than ten tefachim, tzurat hapetach does not help, for even a partition does not help when it is not ten high, and all the more so mere tzurat hapetach. However, if the hollow of the mavo was ten tefachim high and only at the mavo opening it was low less than ten, in this tzurat hapetach helps, provided it was made as required — meaning the reeds were ten tefachim high [Gra]. And know further that if its length was not four amot, the view of several poskim is that its law is like a courtyard, and therefore it is also permitted by a pas of four on one side, or two pasin of mashehuyin on two sides; and likewise the Mechaber himself below in seif 362; and the Mechaber who wrote "only by tzurat hapetach" is not precise:
26:ז: (94) In the height of its hollow, etc. — but if the height of the hollow of the mavo up to the korah is only twenty precise, even though the korah is above twenty, it is valid:
26:ח: (95) Is not permitted by korah — for korah is because of recognition, and above twenty there is no recognition, for the eye does not rule over it; but a lechi, which is close to the ground and suffices at height nineteen — what harm is there if it is very high?:
26:ט: (96) To reduce it from twenty — and the same, he can lower the korah itself and place it within the hollow of the mavo on pegs protruding from the walls below twenty:
26:י: (97) In a structure one tefach wide — and the same for earth of this measure; and one must beware when trodden by feet that it not diminish from the measure in its width; and the same regarding its height, that it not diminish and become more than twenty:
26:כ: (98) In the width of the korah — for its measure is one tefach, as in seif 17; and the reason one tefach width helps is that we hold it is permitted to use beneath the korah, and one standing in that place can see the korah, for at that place it is not higher than twenty, and there is recognition because of this:
26:ל: (99) Must hollow four amot — and that which above one tefach suffices is different here, for in less than ten tefachim it is not called a side at all, and one must make it a side; therefore specifically the measure along the mavo length, which is four amot, is required, as at the beginning of this seif; but there it is called a side, only that it is higher than twenty amot, and therefore one tefach suffices as the measure of wall width (Rashi):
26:מ: (100) Into the mavo — and if he hollowed less than this, he requires specifically a pas of four, or two pasin of two mashehuyin, as the law of a courtyard, as explained at the end of the word "only":
26:נ: (101) Across its entire width — for if a gap remains between the hollowing and the walls, the walls cannot join to it, and it is as if there are no walls for the mavo. However, if the gap between the hollowing and the wall is only less than three tefachim, some say it helps [Peri Megadim]:
26:ס: (102) Two courtyards — the reason for this is that what they permitted in a mavo by lechi and korah is because it has many residents and they do not use it so much for privacy; therefore such a correction suffices; unlike a courtyard, where there are not so many residents, they use it more for privacy, therefore stricter qualification is required — two pasin or a pas of four; and the same for a mavo that does not have two courtyards open into it — few residents and they do private uses in it, therefore lechi and korah do not suffice:
26:ע: (103) And some disagree — for since they can join through the openings, they are considered as one courtyard; and the same for houses open to one another; and Acharonim wrote that since it is a rabbinic matter, we follow the lenient view:
26:פ: (104) And eats in his house — to exclude if his manner of eating is in his father's house:
26:צ: (105) That its length, etc. — for such is the way of a mavo to be:
26:ק: (106) More than its width — even any amount [and its length is called the way of its entry into the mavo, and what is not the way of entry is called width]; for if its length equals its width, it is as a courtyard, as below:
26:ר: (107) One of these — refers to all explained here from "a mavo is not permitted," etc.; and the same law when the mavo length was not four amot:
26:ש: (108) Is not permitted, etc. — for its law is like a courtyard, and therefore for this a pas of four tefachim, etc. is required, as above in seif 2:
26:ת: (109) Or tzurat hapetach — and this helps even when the width is ten, as above in seif 2:
